ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founder, council members, protector, and ultimate beneficial owners against UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and Panama's own National List of PEPs and money laundering predicate offenders under Law 23 of 2015, implementing FATF Recommendation 12 and enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (family members and close associates).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Department of Corporate and Foundation Registration (Registro de Personas Jurídicas), online platform via Sede Electrónica (Internet Portal) of the Government of Panama: https://www.registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All foundation names must be registered in Spanish or in a language expressed in Latin script; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into phonetically equivalent Latin characters; the name must include or be preceded by the word 'Fundación' or 'Foundación', or the abbreviation 'Fdn.', and must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing registered entity in the Republic of Panama; Spanish special characters may be simplified upon transliteration review by the registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed foundation name, the applicant may file a written appeal (recurso de reconsideración) with the Directorship of the Public Registry of Panama within 5 business days of notification, followed by a second appeal (recurso de apelación) with the Board of Directors of the Public Registry within an additional 5 business days; the applicant may simultaneously submit a new name for clearance reserving the right of appeal; the initial name reservation may be renewed for an additional 30-day period upon payment of the applicable fee before the initial 30-day window expires; if the rejection is based on ministerial prohibition of a sensitive token, the applicant must obtain written prior authorization from the relevant ministry or regulator (e.g., Ministerio de Salud or Superintendencia de Bancos) before resubmitting.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permitted for the statutory registered-office requirement as long as the registered agent (Resident Agent and Foundation Agent) maintains a physical address in Panama where legal notices, process service, and official registry communications can be received during normal business hours; however, for an online nutraceuticals e-commerce operation, a mere virtual office may be accepted by the registry but will be reviewed with heightened scrutiny on commercial substance, and may be deemed insufficient by tax authorities or licensing bodies for obtaining a PANAMA MINSA import/health authorization and merchant acquiring licenses, requiring at minimum a contracted local administrative office and a designated local compliance officer.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a High_Risk_Special_License nutraceuticals e-commerce business, the quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA), the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SSRF), and the Dirección de Empresas de Zonas Francas if operating under a special license is approximately 85% within the first 12 months of operation, and 50% within the first 90 days, particularly if the registered office is a virtual address or co-working location.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (Ley N° 25 de 12 de junio de 1995), as amended by Law 45 of 2012; supplementary application of the Commercial Code of Panama for registry and agency matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Mercantile Registry Division.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter executed as a Public Deed (Escritura Pública de Constitución) before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Law 25 of 1995; the Founder must allocate an initial endowment (patrimonio inicial) to the Foundation, typically USD 10,000 or the sum stated in the by-laws. No escrow account is legally mandated for formation, though a Panama bank account is recommended to evidence the endowed assets under AML compliance standards.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Founder, having executed the Foundation Charter under Law 25 of 1995, hereby resolves: 1. Acceptance of Endowment. The initial endowment of USD [.] is assigned to and accepted into the Foundation's patrimony, with receipt acknowledged. 2. Registered Office. The registered office is fixed at [address], Panamá, República de Panamá, with agency of the Resident Agent. 3. Council. [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed Founding Council members; [Name] is designated President and [Name] Secretary-Treasurer. 4. Officers. The Council is granted full authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and confirm the Protector. This resolution is adopted unanimously and effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Execution of Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Notary Public (Notaría Pública) under the Ministry of Government, Notarial Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct foundation counsel to draft the Foundation Charter and by-laws; execute the Charter before a Panamanian Notary; the Notary shall assign the required notarial ledger entry and authorize the public deed in Spanish.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter and by-laws
Passport copy of the Founder
Proof of registered address / utility bill
Identity details of Founding Council members
Name availability certificate (certificado de no inscripción) from the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary issues a query (reparo), amend the inconsistent clauses and re-execute the deed; pay any statutory document stamps before re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of Foundation Charter in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Mercantile Registry Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original public deed and the application for inscription (solicitud de inscripción); pay the assessed registration fee at the registry payment windows or via the official online portal; await issuance of the inscribed certificate.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública)
Inscription application form
Assessment and fee receipt
Legalization of signatures where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Within the term granted by the Registry, cure any noted defect (obstáculo) or respond to the Registrar's observation in writing to obtain final inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directorate General of Revenues (Dirección General de Ingresos - DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the taxpayer registration for the Foundation and obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente); obtain the digital tax signature (firma electrónica) through the National Authority for Government Innovation (AIG) to enable e-filing.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
DGI taxpayer registration form (Formulario 20)
Passport copy of the Resident Agent and Council members
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI questions economic substance, submit a declaration confirming the foundation's assets, banking relations, and business purpose to close the file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá), Directorate of Sales and Collections
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the aviso de operación for the administrative/warehouse address, pay the municipal business tax (tasa municipal), and obtain the municipal operating license covering the e-commerce retail activity.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate of the Foundation
Certified copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
Lease agreement or proof of ownership of premises
Fire safety inspection certificate (if premises are occupied)
Omni-civil identification of the person in charge
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality assesses accumulated taxes or flags address inconsistencies, pay the corrected fees or amend the aviso within the granted term and re-present the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Health of Panama (Ministerio de Salud - MINSA), National Directorate of Pharmacies and Drugs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit each dietary supplement SKU for sanitary registration (Registro Sanitario de Productos) under Executive Decree No. 51 of 25 October 2005, including product technical files, labeling, and shelf-life data; obtain the registration certificate before commercial import and online sale in Panama.
required_dossiers: Complete product technical file and formula
Certificate of free sale from country of origin
Final label artwork in Spanish
Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) certificate of manufacturer
Foundation RUC and registered address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to MINSA's exigency letter with additional stability, heavy metals, and microbiological assay data; if denied, file an administrative appeal (recurso de reconsideración) within the statutory term.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health of Panama (Ministerio de Salud - MINSA), National Directorate of Pharmacies and Drugs; Municipality of Panama for the commercial operating license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Sanitary Registration of Dietary Supplements (Registro Sanitario de Productos) and Municipal Commercial Operating License (Aviso de Operación).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (Ministerio de Ambiente - MiAMBIENTE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category I: a pure e-commerce fulfillment warehouse storing pre-packaged supplements triggers only registration with MiAMBIENTE, not a full Environmental Impact Assessment study, provided there is no manufacturing, effluent generation, or waste incineration on site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with Executive Decree No. 8 of 2012 for sanitary effluents (BOD, COD, and pH limits) where a restroom and drainage exist; VOCs: none reasonably expected from sealed supplement bottles, but flash-point documentation required for any stored liquids; Solid waste: segregation and municipal collection per Law 22 of 2016 on municipal solid waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá; structural load review of pallet racking and shelving per the local building code; MINSA hygienic-sanitary inspection of the storage area as suitable for food and dietary supplement handling; registration with the State Industrial Accident Insurance Fund (INARE/Instituto Nacional de Riesgos Ambientales) for occupational coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; online portal: e-Tax 2.0 / SEDI at https://www.dgi.gob.pa; customs interface through Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Appoint a licensed resident agent (agente residente) and a Panamanian fiscal representative. Step 2: Obtain a qualified electronic signature (Firma Electrónica) from an ANATI-accredited certification provider. Step 3: File the Foundation Charter (Pacto Fundacional) and Regulations with the Registro Público de Panamá; minimum capital B/. 10,000 with at least B/. 2,500 paid-in (Law 25 of 1995). Step 4: Submit the RUC inscription via SEDI or at the DGI collectorate of the registered office, attaching: certified copy of the Public Registry inscription, foundation regulations, notarized appointment of the fiscal representative, and proof of the registered agent. Step 5: Declare the economic activity under CIIU 4791.10 and select the ITBMS liability status. Step 6: Obtain the definitive 16-digit RUC certificate and enroll in the electronic invoicing system (SFT or accredited billing provider). Step 7: Complete municipal Aviso de Operación registration and, where relevant, file the MINSA supplement e-commerce license application. Estimated DGI processing: 15 business days; complete procurement 3–6 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or pass-through election exists for Panamanian PIFs. Available elections: (a) optional small-taxpayer integrated regime (Régimen Tributario Integrado) for gross annual revenue ≤ B/. 75,000, consolidating ITBMS, income tax, and municipal obligations; (b) election to fix the PIF duration (determinate term up to 50 years or indefinite); (c) voluntary registration as an indirect tax collector for digital services under Ley 131 de 2020 where relevant; (d) group consolidation election for income tax under Ley 62 de 2018; (e) option to claim limited foreign tax credits on Panamanian-source income; (f) election to treat a PIF as a closed company for dividend remittance purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — VAT-equivalent under Articles 1057–1138 of the Código Fiscal
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General ITBMS regime: no minimum turnover threshold; registration is mandatory before the first taxable operation. Simplified small-taxpayer regime: optional up to B/. 75,000 annual gross revenue; where the PIF's cross-border supplement sales exceed B/. 75,000, the general regime with monthly or semi-monthly filings applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica en Línea) under the DGI framework (Law 62 of 2018 and implementing DGI regulations). Each invoice is validated and fiscally sealed by the SFT (Servicio de Facturación Transmisible) or by an accredited billing provider; a digital fiscal seal, QR code, and unique CONC authorization number are required. Transmission must use REST API (JSON/XML over HTTPS); no offline batch stamping is permitted except during a DGI-authorized 48-hour contingency window. Export invoices must include the DUA reference and the zero-rate reason code 'Exportacion'.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% ITBMS applies to physical goods (including dietary supplement e-commerce orders) where: (a) title and risk pass to a non-resident buyer; (b) goods physically depart Panama within 90 days of the invoice date; (c) the export is evidenced by an accepted DUA in the ANA single window; and (d) ancillary services (freight, handling, packing) are supplied to non-residents for use outside Panama. For nutraceuticals, the MINSA sanitary registration for the exported product and a lot-specific sanitary export certificate must support each customs filing; absence of MINSA clearance voids the zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Declaración Única de Aduanas) accepted and stamped by ANA
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or courier master waybill evidencing physical departure from Panamanian territory

Inward Remittance Certificate (comprobante de ingreso de divisas) issued by the receiving Panamanian bank or the high-risk merchant account settlement statement tracing credit-card receipts to the foreign issuing bank
Commercial invoice with HS code (e.g., HS 2106.90 for supplement preparations) and the destination-country address of the non-resident purchaser
Packing list and purchase order or sales contract reflecting Incoterms EXW/FOB and foreign buyer identity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may audit export zero-rating for five tax years, extended to ten years in cases of non-filing or fraud. A disallowed zero-rating triggers reassessment at 7% ITBMS plus the omitted tax surcharge of 25% to 150%, statutory moratorium interest, and possible customs fines of B/. 10,000–B/. 100,000. Criminal exposure under Law 76 of 2019: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years where evasion exceeds B/. 50,000 and 5 to 10 years where evasion exceeds B/. 100,000. The anti-avoidance rule of Article 762-A of the Fiscal Code allows DGI to disregard the PIF's separate patrimony where the foundation is used abusively, and ANA may revoke the exporter's license on the VUPA single window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — Panama does not maintain a central bank; the US dollar is legal tender and the economy is fully dollarized. Banking supervision is conducted by SBP, monetary stability is effectively anchored by the US Federal Reserve, and AML/CFT oversight is reinforced by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama imposes no exchange controls; the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) exists only as a bookkeeping denomination at parity with the USD and is not physically issued. Current and capital accounts are fully convertible; profit remittance, dividends, interest, and royalties may be freely repatriated without central bank approval or withholding of an exchange nature. Banking filings may require a transaction concept/purpose code solely for statistical reporting, not regulatory restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in USD or any freely convertible currency in local or foreign banks. No timeline applies for repatriation or conversion; however, invoices and bank credit evidence should be retained for transfer-pricing and tax-territoriality substantiation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Legal Representative Escrow and Operating Combined

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium viability. Panama does not license dedicated 'Electronic Money Institutions' (EMIs) as independent deposit takers. Offshore digital EMIs and payment processors must operate through a SBP-licensed bank sponsor or hold a foreign (e.g., EU) EMI license while cooperating with a Panamanian clearing bank. For a Private Interest Foundation engaged in high-risk nutraceutical e-commerce, a pure EMI structure will not provide the required treasury certainty; a SBP-regulated commercial bank account remains mandatory for settlement, although specialized payment/acquiring partners registered with the Superintendencia de Bancos can be appended to the banking rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For non-resident, beneficial-ownership-complex Private Interest Foundations, most tier-1 banks require a physical or video-conference interview with the foundation council (board) members, registered and beneficial owners, and the resident agent. Remote onboarding is permissible in practice, but enhanced due diligence is always elevated for cross-border nutraceuticals. The default commercial position is: (1) if beneficial owners hold non-high-risk nationality and are established corporate executives, a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney with live video interview is accepted; (2) if the business involves direct-to-consumer e-commerce with high chargeback/AML flags, physical attendance at a Panama branch is expected by the compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation legal form disregarded by correspondent banks; hidden beneficial ownership of foundation council and protector
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full apostilled Foundation Charter, current Council Resolution appointing officers, a foundation register extract issued by the Public Registry, an organizational chart identifying all settlors, council members, protectors, registered agents and beneficiaries, plus sworn declarations of source-of-funds (SOF) and source-of-wealth (SOW).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk ISIC 4791: retail sale of dietary supplements and nutraceuticals online — health product claims and cross-border merchant exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PANAMA Ministry of Health importation approval where applicable, product ingredient certification, establishment certificate for e-commerce operations, licensee evidence for the statutory supplement trading permit, compliance policy on medical claims and prohibited ingredients, and third-party laboratory certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Excessive cross-border transaction flows into a low-corporate-tax jurisdiction with no clear physical commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or virtual office contract, supply-chain agreements, warehouse or 3PL logistics contracts, customer database anonymization and KYC process, contracts between the foundation and suppliers, plus evidence of commercial substance such as a local General Administration Office, email domain, and monthly operational expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customer chargeback and fraud risk from online card-present-not acceptance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chargeback and refund policy, 3-D Secure protocol execution, PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance certificate, cardholder dispute escalation procedure, and reconciliation report from the acquiring bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) or sanctions screening mismatches in beneficial owner list
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated daily sanctions and PEP screening system logs, certified 'Negative PEP' confirmation from a licensed Panama law firm, International Compliance Certification of the foundation, and confirmation that all directors/councils have not served in public office within last 12 months.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All incoming capital from shareholders or the settlor should be remitted via SWIFT MT103 for high-value transactions; for verified capital contributions, include payment details stating 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION TO PIF' and, if applicable, reference the Foundation Charter clause. Panama applies no exchange control, so conversion into USD is performed automatically at the receiving bank using the fixed 1:1 balboa peg. Correspondent banks may require a transaction code; agreed code can be 'A110 – Commercial / Bussiness' or 'A10 General Commercial Goods' when injecting trade-related working capital. To prevent money-laundering red flags, capital injection must be disaggregated: (1) funding of operations is labeled 'trade prepayment / goods inventory financing'; (2) emergency operational reserve is labeled 'intercompany loan under foundation account'; and both must have an authenticated bank statement of the remitter.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and logistics payments out of Panama use the SWIFT global clearing rail, predominantly through MT103 single-customer credit transfers. For larger purchase orders, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) through an SBP-licensed bank is permissible; the favorable jurisdiction is USD-denominated confirming bank. Trade disbursements should be allocated among: (1) MT103 transfers to verified foreign suppliers for inventory purchases; (2) ACH Panama / Fedwire for domestic USD settlement if the supplier maintains a Panamanian account; (3) Commercial L/C (UCP600) for bulk pharmaceutical raw material import, with Ben10/Be88 process handled by the bank. Direct disbursement to a third-party beneficiary without invoice back-up is not recommended.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD is the functional currency; no PAB transfer risk, so FX hedging is only necessary when entering receivables or payables in EUR, CHF, GBP, CNY, or AED.
Spot FX trades: fully permissible through SBP-licensed banks and correspondents.
Outright FX Forwards (delivery-based): permitted for institutional clients when executed with a bank license; the conversion is settled through the bank, no exchange-control clearing required.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): not locally available for PAB/USD because of full dollarization, but available to manage CNY/EUR emerging-market exposures through international desks at Citibank, Banistmo, or BAC.
Currency Swaps (XCY): permissible subject to bank approval and used exclusively for trade-portfolio adjustments.
Options (FX vanillas): permitted with international broker-dealers; no Panamanian product only restriction for off-exchange derivative within banking relationship.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Flat Franchise Tax of the Private Interest Foundation (Tasa Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado, Ley 25 de 1995)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – payment effected at Banco Nacional de Panamá or Caja de Ahorros; compliance monitored by the Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry) against the foundation folio
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar fiscal year (within the first three months following 31 December) for a PIF maintained on a calendar-year basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment recargo of 5% on the unpaid annual tax plus default interest at the DGI legal rate (1.5% per month or fraction); the foundation's public folio is marked 'Pendiente', blocking issuance of Paz y Salvo tax-clearance certificates; continued non-payment for five consecutive fiscal years triggers administrative strike-off (cancelación de oficio) by the Registro Público, extinguishing the PIF's legal personality and jeopardizing merchant accounts and bank balances

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada Anual de Renta, Formulario 150) including issuance of the foundation's financial statements as supporting annex
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – e-filing via the DGI taxpayer portal (Sede Electrónica)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 31 August for the fiscal year ending 31 December under the DGI's RUC-digit filing calendar (the statutory three-month rule is superseded by the annual DGI resolution establishing an extended exclusive e-filing window between June and August); an active PIF with an RUC must file even if all e-commerce revenue is foreign-source and produces a nil Panama tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine from USD 25 to USD 500 per return, increased to 10% of the tax due where tax is outstanding; monthly default interest of 1.5% on unpaid balances; the DGI may proceed with de-oficio assessment, suspend the RUC, and include the PIF in the taxpayer default registry, which can escalate to a strike-off recommendation for the foundation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial-Ownership Confirmation and UBO Register Update (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) filed by the resident agent on the DGI UBO portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Registro de Beneficiarios Finales; supporting AML/KYC file retained on-site by the registered agent under Law 23 of 2015
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in foundation council membership, protector appointment, beneficiary class, or transfer of foundation economic rights; where no change occurs, the resident agent performs an annual no-change re-confirmation of the UBO dataset on or before 31 March of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines between USD 1,000 and USD 10,000 per violation under AML Law 23/2015 for missing or stale UBO filings; the DGI may flag the PIF's RUC as non-compliant, and the resident agent is contractually and legally obligated to terminate services if beneficial-ownership data remain unconfirmed, exposing the foundation to loss of registered status and strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Operation Permit and Patent Renewal (Aviso de Operación y Patente Municipal) – only applicable where the PIF maintains a commercial premise or fulfillment point inside a Panamanian municipality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal treasury (Tesorería/Rentas Municipales) of the Municipality where the premises are located, e.g., Municipio de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal on or before 31 January of each calendar year; a PIF conducting pure cross-border e-commerce with no physical establishment or local fulfillment activity in Panama has no municipal patent exposure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal fines of up to USD 1,000 plus administrative closure of unlicensed commercial premises; inability to obtain the municipal Paz y Salvo may additionally block renewal of the DGI RUC and Import/Health operating certificates

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent financial statement audit by a CPA registered in Panama is mandatory when the PIF's annual gross income reaches or exceeds USD 1,000,000 (B/.1,000,000) or when required by specific DGI order under Código Fiscal Article 703; a dietary-supplement e-commerce PIF processing credit-card payments will also face an audited-statement covenant from high-risk merchant acquirers even below the statutory threshold
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panamanian statutory accounting is IFRS (NIIF) as adopted by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos de Panamá; a small PIF may apply IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para las PYMES); Panama's territorial tax regime limits the Formulario 150 tax base to Panama-source income, requiring careful sourcing analysis of fulfilment location and contracting counterparties for cross-border supplement sales

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% final corporate income tax (ISR - Impuesto Sobre la Renta) on net Panamanian-source taxable income; no tax on foreign-source income under Panama's territorial tax doctrine.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) under Law 25 of 1995 are statutorily exempt from corporate income tax, dividend tax, and net-worth tax when the foundation's assets are located outside Panama and its activities are performed outside Panama. The effective Panama tax burden for a fully offshore e-commerce PIF is limited to the annual government franchise fee (USD 300) plus the Resident Agent fee. No CFC rules apply to PIF beneficiaries. Qualifying small taxpayers may elect the one-rate simplified regime ('Régimen de Tasa Única') for gross revenue up to USD 200,000, producing an effective tax burden well below the 25% headline rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 745 (Declaración Jurada de Renta - Legal Entities) filed through Panama's DGI electronic portal (DGI-RENTA / e-Tax), supplemented by Form 780 (Annual Beneficial Owner and Shareholder Report) under Law 52 of 2016 and, where applicable, Form 733 (Transfer Pricing Informative Return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Monthly CAIR advance prepayments (Complementary Activity Tax, generally 2% of gross Panamanian-source billings) are due during the fiscal year for taxpayers in the general regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three (3) months after the fiscal year-end. Standard fiscal years ending 31 December are due by 31 March; companies electing a 30 June year-end file by 30 September. Payment of any tax due accompanies the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) assigned by the DGI to the foundation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the PIF's RUC issued at formation; quote the Resident Agent's registration reference. Non-resident founders must ensure the RUC remains active and the Resident Agent is current with annual fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the taxable year covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use 01-Jan to 31-Dec unless the foundation elected a different 12-month period. Foreign-managed foundations should keep a consistent election and mirror the period on all supporting bank and payment-rail statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 - Ingresos Gravables de Fuente Panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue sourced in Panama subject to the 25% ISR (e.g., online sales delivered to Panama or services performed in Panama).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report zero if all e-commerce sales are concluded and delivered abroad. Do not net costs or payment-rail charges; attach the platform settlement reports if a Panama-source nexus is disputed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 - Ingresos Exentos y No Sujetos (Foreign-Source Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source revenues, offshore investment gains, and capital gains realized outside Panama that qualify for territorial exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule listing foreign-platform settlements (Stripe, PayPal, card acquirer payouts), foreign warehouse documentation, and bank statements. Include a sworn declaration by the foundation council that the assets, management, and activities are situated outside Panama, invoking Article 4 of Law 25 of 1995.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable profit from Panamanian-source revenue after allowable deductions and the resulting 25% income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an exempt PIF, enter zero and cite the Law 25 of 1995 exemption in the observation field. If any Panamanian-source revenue exists, the full 25% ISR applies and the PIF tax exemption is lost for that portion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for monthly CAIR advance payments and any Panamanian withholding taxes suffered during the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit only Panamanian CAIR payments and Panamanian WHT. Foreign VAT, GST, or foreign income taxes are not creditable against Panamanian ISR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sworn signature of the legal representative and a Panama-licensed CPA, including the CPA's professional ID number ('Idoneidad') and stamp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident administrators must retain a Panama-licensed CPA to sign the return. Electronic filing requires the CPA's DGI digital certificate; late signature or incomplete CPA data invalidates the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction thereof, capped at 100% of the tax, plus monthly indexation interest (approximately 1.5% per month). Failure to file an exempt/informative return triggers fixed administrative fines ranging from USD 250 to USD 5,000. The DGI may embargo bank accounts, suspend the RUC digital certificate, impose a tax lien, and refuse the solvencia fiscal clearance required for renewing merchant accounts, sanitary permits, and the Resident Agent's services. Fraudulent returns carry criminal liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final dividend withholding tax on dividends or beneficiary distributions paid out of Panamanian-source profits of a Panamanian legal entity (Fiscal Code, dividend withholding regime). Distributions by a PIF from foreign-source assets are not subject to Panama dividend WHT; however, dividends paid by a Panamanian company to the PIF remain subject to the 10% WHT at the source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama maintains a limited DTA network (including Korea, Singapore, UAE, Qatar, Mexico, the Netherlands, Portugal, and others in force or in negotiation). To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction's competent authority; (ii) deliver to the Panamanian withholding agent, prior to payment, a beneficial-ownership declaration, a copy of the DTA article, and the PIF foundation deed with legalized Spanish translation; (iii) instruct the withholding agent to apply the reduced rate at source; and (iv) retain the complete file for DGI inspection. If the reduced rate was not applied at source, the non-resident must file a refund claim ('Solicitud de Devolución') with the DGI within the three-year statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 12.5% statutory Panama-source WHT on interest paid to non-residents (exemptions apply to interbank deposits and certain export financing); treaty rates commonly 0-5%. Royalties: 12.5% statutory WHT on Panama-source royalties for IP, trademarks, know-how, and technical services; treaty rates generally 5-10% depending on the DTA. Payments must be supported by definitive contracts and, for royalties, by evidence of actual use of the intangible in Panama.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama's transfer pricing rules (effective 2012) require a Local File and the annual TP Informative Return (Form 733) when the taxpayer's gross revenue exceeds USD 3,000,000 (B/. 3,000,000) in the corresponding fiscal year, or when cross-border related-party transactions exceed this threshold. Regardless of the threshold, any PIF purchasing supplements from related manufacturers abroad must apply arm's length pricing and retain contemporaneous documentation of the pricing policy, intercompany agreements, and benchmark analysis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama enacted economic substance legislation (Law 254 of 2021 and implementing regulations) applicable to legal entities and foundations performing 'Relevant Activities' - including distribution, logistics, financing, IP holding, and headquarters services - within Panama. A PIF administering a cross-border nutraceutical e-commerce business from abroad will not need Panamanian substance; however, if the foundation has Panamanian premises, local employees, or locally managed decision-making, it must demonstrate core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Panama, adequate staff and premises, and local board minutes. Non-compliance exposes the foundation to fines up to USD 1,000,000, potential reclassification of tax residence, and revocation of the exemption under Law 25 of 1995. The Resident Agent must keep the statutory registers (foundation deed, beneficial owners, and asset register) physically available in Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Reporting income as foreign-source when the e-commerce activity actually produces Panamanian-source revenue (e.g., goods stored in or delivered from a Panama warehouse, payment processing executed through a Panama acquiring bank, or local marketing services performed in Panama). Also, deliberately omitting DGI registration and filing to avoid ISR on online sales to Panama residents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of up to three times the evaded tax, monthly indexation interest on the unpaid balance, embargo of bank accounts, and publication of defaulters. Criminal conviction for tax fraud (defraudación fiscal) under the Panamanian Penal Code carries imprisonment of two (2) to five (5) years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Members of the foundation council, the founder, and the Resident Agent are jointly and severally liable when they willfully sign or cause a false return to be filed. Courts may pierce the corporate veil and order civil restitution of the evaded tax with interest; criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment and a preventive travel ban (prohibición de salida del país).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a PIF with no real economic substance solely as an invoicing pass-through or concealment vehicle for a non-resident online pharmacy; maintaining no accounting records, no beneficiary register, or an anonymous beneficial owner structure in violation of Law 25 of 1995 and Law 52 of 2016; and holding the PIF out as an operating company while all decisions are made by an undisclosed third party.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to USD 1,000,000 under the economic substance and AML regimes; cancellation of the foundation's registration; the DGI may recharacterize the PIF as a transparent entity and assess tax directly against the founder or beneficial owner; the Public Registry may refuse renewals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Judicial piercing of the corporate veil allows creditors and the State to seize the personal assets of the founder, protector, and council members for foundation liabilities. False declarations before the Public Registry constitute false-oath offenses, and the DGI may pursue criminal charges with imprisonment up to eight (8) years for aggravated fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting credit-card payments for high-risk nutraceutical sales without an AML compliance program, failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner of the merchant account, structuring sales in amounts below record-keeping thresholds to evade reporting, or concealing the merchant's true business model from the acquiring bank and the Panama Superintendency of Banks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Law 23 of 2015 (AML/CFT) carries administrative fines up to USD 1,000,000 for legal entities; money laundering under Article 254 of the Penal Code is punishable by five (5) to twelve (12) years of imprisonment. The Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF) may freeze accounts without prior court order for renewable periods, and the acquiring bank may terminate the merchant agreement and file a Suspicious Activity Report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Council members and the signatories of the merchant application are criminally liable if they knew or should have known that funds derived from unlicensed or fraudulent activity. The Public Prosecutor's Office may impose an international travel ban (Nota de Impedimento) and order provisional seizure of personal assets pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling dietary supplements, nutraceuticals, or products classified as medicines or health products in Panama without the prior sanitary registration of the Ministry of Health (Registro Sanitario de Medicamentos y Alimentos - RSA), or obtaining a high-risk merchant account through false representations of the business as a low-risk general retail operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative closure of the business (clausura), withdrawal of any sanitary licenses, and fines ranging from USD 5,000 to USD 50,000 under Panama's sanitary law. The acquiring bank may terminate the Merchant Agreement, blacklist the merchant, and report the misrepresentation to the Superintendency of Banks; criminal liability arises for the illegal exercise of pharmacy if the products contain controlled substances, punishable by three (3) to six (6) years of imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The individuals signing the merchant application, the foundation council, and the Resident Agent may be jointly sued for fraud, unfair trade practice, and unjust enrichment. Criminal conviction leads to imprisonment, permanent disqualification from serving as a Panama corporate officer or Resident Agent, and civil restitution to consumers and financial institutions.
